full_judgment: 3. The case of the plaintiffs described in the plaint in short is that, one, Hira Lai Agorwala belonged to part of the suit land measuring an area of 1.79 acres by virtue of several registered deeds dated back to 1936 and 1953 and accordingly, his name was prepared in the RS record and thereby he acquired title and possession over the said property. Apart from that, the said Hira Lal Agorwala and his cousin named, Gourishankar Agorwala purchased 22 decimals of land from RS Plot No. 953 by registered kabala dated 18-6-1988 and thereby, they started enjoying title and possession over that 22 decimals of land proportionately by erecting homestead thereon. Subsequently, Hira Lala Agorwala sold out 5½ decimals of land out of his share of 11 decimals of land in RS Plot No. 953 to Gourishankar Agorwala by way of gift. It has further been stated that, the wife of Hira Lal Agorwala, Fulia BieAgorwala took defendant No. 2 as her adopted son. While Hira Lal Agorwala had been enjoying title and possession over 1.79 acres of land he proposed be settle (pattan) the same to the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 3-5, Gourishankar fixing the consideration (salami) at Taka 6,001 and the yearly rent at Taka 28 and it was executed on 4th Ashar, 1360 BS through amalnama and dakhila. Subsequently, Gourishankar Agorwala died leaving behind the plaintiff, the predecessor of the opposite-parties as well as defendant Nos. 3-5. It has further been stated that, after getting that 1.79 acres of land, Gourishankar Agorwala started enjoying title and possession over that property by giving rent to different tenants where there remained several shops and thus acquired indefeasible title and possession over the settled land. It has also been stated that, Shib Lal Agorwala, defendant No. 2 is not the adopted son of Hira Lal Agorwala and Hira Lal Agorwala was older than that of Gourishankar Agorwala when Gourishankar Agorwala devolved the responsibility upon Hira Lal Agorwala to get his name prepared in the SA record in respect of the suit land but ultimately it has not been recorded in his name in spite of taking settlement from Hira Lal Agorwala and therefore, the suit land was wrongly prepared in the name of Hira Lal Agorwala in SA record alone. The defendant No. 2 has never acquired any property left by Gourishartkar Agorwala and in the aforesaid way plaintiff is entitled to 1/4 share left by his father, Gourishankar Agorwala and when the plaintiff requested the defendants to partition the suit property on 2nd Chaitra, 1399 BS corresponding to 16-5-1992 AD, the defendants denied to partition the same and hence the suit.
